biomarkers.name: CRLF2 rearrangements (IGH-CRLF2, P2RY8-CRLF2)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Often co-occurs with JAK-STAT alterations, especially JAK2 mutations. JAK inhibitors (for example ruxolitinib) are under clinical investigation

biomarkers.name: JAK2 rearrangements / mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: JAK-pathway targeted therapy is under clinical investigation

biomarkers.name: ABL-class fusions (ABL1, ABL2, PDGFRB, CSF1R)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Often TKI-sensitive (for example imatinib or dasatinib); comprehensive fusion testing is essential

biomarkers.name: Gene expression profiling (Ph-like signature)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic classifier used to identify the subtype in conjunction with genomic testing

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: B-ALL morphology (as per B_ALL); gene expression profile similar to Ph+ ALL but BCR-ABL1 negative
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; genomic subtype guides targeted therapy

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: B-cell precursor with gene expression profile similar to Ph+ ALL but BCR-ABL1 negative
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Distinct molecular subgroups drive the Ph-like phenotype through parallel kinase activation, including CRLF2-rearranged disease (often with JAK-STAT alterations, ~50%), ABL-class fusions (~10-15%, often TKI-sensitive), JAK-STAT alterations, and other kinase-activating alterations; IKZF1 deletions are common
